At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built. We offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to data How can you make a difference? UNICEF works to ensure that every child has the right to learn, develop and participate fully, without discrimination. Advancing equity, gender equality and inclusion is central to this mandate, with a particular focus on children who are most marginalized or excluded from education systems, including children with disabilities, girls, children affected by poverty, displacement, conflict and crisis, and children who are out of school or at risk of exclusion. Within UNICEF Global Programme Division, the Education Practice works to strengthen education systems so that they are more equitable, inclusive, gender-responsive, and resilient across the life course. This includes supporting countries to improve policy and planning, financing, data and evidence, teacher and workforce development, accessible and inclusive learning environments, and cross-sectoral coordination for children’s learning, development, and wellbeing in development and emergency contexts Global evidence increasingly shows that most children are in school – yet learning levels remain low, with an estimated six out of ten children in low income counties unable to read and understand a simple sentence by the age of ten. National, regional and global assessments continue to tell the same story of poor learning outcomes, pointing to inefficiencies in education systems, misallocated resources and insufficiently targeted policies. UNICEF is committed to supporting governments and partners in ensuring that all children acquire foundational learning skills, including foundational literacy, numeracy, and socio-emotional competencies. Achieving this goal requires not only the availability of timely, high-quality learning assessment data but also the effective use of that data to inform policies, programmes, and teaching and learning practices. UNICEF is looking to engage an independent consultant to work with Ministries of Education and regional bodies in translating evidence to action and to inform policies, plans and strategies. The consultant will support national teams to unpack large scale national and international assessments, identify areas to strengthen, and support advocacy efforts around teacher training, curriculum revision and resource allocation. It is expected that the consultant will work with international datasets (SEA-PLM, PASEC, PISA etc) as well as national and even classroom-level datasets and/or systems. The work will build on prior work such as SEA-PLM Initiative 2, while also exploring new data needs with countries. A strong focus is expected on the applicability of the analysis and information to classroom level practice, including with an equity lens. The consultant will develop tools and guidance related to evidence-based policy and decision making. This includes supporting analysis for SDG reporting and interpreting international and regional guidelines, including for emergency and fragile contexts. The consultant will also build national capacity to analyze, interpret and use data and evidence for improved policy making. supporting improved learning outcomes for all children If you would like to know more about this consultancy, please review the complete Terms of Reference here: ToRTMC0005700.pdf To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have...
